title: Quick check: Backend-for-Frontend Architecture

questions.prompt: In the context of “Backend-for-Frontend Architecture” and “What a backend-for-frontend layer is”, Which file convention defines an App Router HTTP endpoint?
options: A `layout.jsx` file that exports a React component.
A `route.js` file in the route segment.
questions.answer_key: A `route.js` file in the route segment.
questions.explanation: Route Handlers use the `route.js`/`route.ts` convention and implement HTTP methods explicitly.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Backend-for-Frontend Architecture”, What is a key difference between direct server-side data fetching and a Route Handler?
options: A Server Component can often call trusted data functions directly, while a Route Handler exposes an HTTP endpoint.
A Route Handler is always required for every server-side database query.
A Route Handler is a stylesheet convention.
Server Components cannot access server-side data.
questions.answer_key: A Server Component can often call trusted data functions directly, while a Route Handler exposes an HTTP endpoint.
questions.explanation: Avoid unnecessary internal HTTP round trips when direct server-side data access fits the architecture.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Backend-for-Frontend Architecture”, How should an external webhook be processed?
options: Trust any JSON request with an event name.
Process duplicate deliveries as new payments every time.
Verify its signature, validate the event, and make processing idempotent for retries or duplicates.
Expose the signing secret in a public response.
questions.answer_key: Verify its signature, validate the event, and make processing idempotent for retries or duplicates.
questions.explanation: Webhook requests require sender verification, safe event handling, and duplicate-delivery protection.
